newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks finish firmer as futures fly.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks finish firmer as futures fly.

text.p: Australian shares closed just firmer on Wednesday with futures-linked buying in the afternoon lifting the market back to better than square for the day.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 0.9 points higher at 2,433.0.
The March share price index futures contract was up 17 points at 2,435, a two point premium to the index.

While the market dipped early on nervousness ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, due later today, brokers said strong demand for the leaders emerged late in the day as futures flew home.
"There has been hectic trade in the SPI and that has pulled the leaders out of the hole," said a dealer from a Sydney-based brokerage.
"BHP, CRA and the banks all had big comebacks. That discount has narrowed quite a bit since Monday so I think you have seen some arbitrage play going on."
Other traders agreed, saying there appeared to be a lack of real reasons for the change in sentiment late in the day.

"Somebody is trading between the markets with some quite good volumes," said broker Grant Williams of Reynolds and Co, although he noted that the early weakness had been more than most expected in any case.
December quarter GDP figures were largely in line with expectations and failed to have much impact.
Oil and gas major Woodside Petroleum jumped 31.7 cents to close at its day's high of A$8.977 (US$7.09) after its 58 percent higher full year net profit of A$190.96 million.

Building materials group, Boral, added six cents to A$3.50 after its first half net profit of A$93.16 million, while fellow building materials group, Pioneer International, was active with 7.7 million shares traded, the bulk in three lines totalling six million though Merrill Lynch. Pioneer shares closed six cents higher at A$3.97.
Financial services group Tyndall Australia closed three cents higher at A$1.98 after announcing a 29 percent higher full year net profit of A$22.07 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 29 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
